results.summary_before: This project is an 8-bit floating-point unit in FP8 E4M3 format, implementing 18 operations including add, subtract, multiply, divide, square root, comparisons, and integer conversions, with support for five IEEE rounding modes. The core is a pipelined, elastic datapath with variable-latency divide and sqrt, and it uses a byte-stream interface with independent valid/ready handshakes to multiplex the wide internal datapath onto the limited Tiny Tapeout pins. The design has been exhaustively verified against a reference model for all 1,843,968 input combinations at both RTL and gate level. No external hardware is required; any host that can drive the handshake pins and data bus can operate the FPU.

results.summary_before: This project is a single int8 multiply-accumulate unit that computes the dot product of two signed 8-bit vectors by time-multiplexing operands onto an 8-bit input port. It uses a two-state FSM to alternately capture an operand and then multiply-accumulate, and reads out a 24-bit accumulator over two clock cycles by using both the dedicated and bidirectional output pins. The design is a fundamental building block for neural network accelerators, and its operation is verified by feeding component pairs and reading the accumulated result, with overlapping output windows providing error checking. No external hardware is required, though a host must drive the inputs and read the outputs according to the phase timing.

results.summary_before: The HDC Classifier is an 8-bit hyperdimensional computing classifier that compares an input vector against two class prototypes and selects the class with the smaller Hamming distance. Input data arrives on the eight input pins, while mode, class selection, valid and start controls are driven on the bidirectional pins and the six-bit distance, winner and done signals appear on the outputs. The workflow is to reset, present data and control signals, assert start, then read the winner and distance once done is high. No external hardware is required beyond the standard clock and reset, and the documentation is brief but sufficient for the interface.

results.summary_before: This design performs streaming pixel-based face detection by classifying skin tone and counting dark pixels in eye, nose, and mouth zones. Pixels are input serially one channel at a time, along with channel select, pixel valid, frame done, and zone metadata. At the end of a frame, it evaluates conditions and outputs detection flags. Testing requires a MATLAB preprocessing script to convert images into a pixel stream, and the design is intended to be driven by a microcontroller or cocotb testbench.

results.summary_before: This is a fully-differential Class-AB folded-cascode operational amplifier implemented in SKY130A. It achieves 100.3 dB open-loop gain, 9.34 MHz GBW, and 0.71 mW power consumption, with an on-chip bias generator requiring only two external bias voltages. The amplifier is tested in a closed-loop configuration with external resistors and a differential signal source. Notable limitations include non-rail-to-rail output and reduced phase margin at low temperatures.

results.summary_before: VITAL-AP is an adaptive 8-bit pixel register designed for low-power image and video processing, deciding whether to update or hold its value based on pixel value, transition magnitude, temporal behavior, edge activity, and motion activity. It aims to reduce switching activity and dynamic power by suppressing unnecessary updates, with controls for sensitivity, prediction enable, force update, and various awareness modes. The design can be tested with provided Verilog and Cocotb testbenches covering static, small, and large transitions, sequences, and force-update. It is a research-oriented project, but no silicon results are reported.
